documents.title: OAI's Guidance for Fall 2024: AI & Academic Integrity
documents.summary: The Office of Academic Integrity's Fall 2024 slides say there is no university-wide AI policy, quote Academic Integrity Code provisions on exams, attribution and hallucinations, and advise instructors on writing course policies. They also explain why OAI does not use detectors and how faculty must route suspected misuse to OAI.
documents.stance_why: The document states 'Faculty are responsible for determining what use of generative AI tools, if any, is appropriate in their courses' and that there is 'no AI policy that applies to the entire university system'; it offers three sample templates (strict, limited, open) rather than one stance.

notes: Interim guidance text is a partial WebFetch extract (5 quotes), so coded from those only. The OAI deck also reproduces example syllabus statements from other institutions (UT Tyler, TWU, Ontario Tech, Macalester, UCSC, Texas A&M, Colgate, GWU, Penn, SUNY Albany); the deck says these are not AU policy, so they were not coded as units. OAI tier templates are listed in tiers; stance set to delegates.
